messages:
alex: Heads up — after the kernel-autoselect rollout yesterday we're seeing 95th pct latency spikes for short sequences (<64) on A100s. nvprof heatmap shows a bunch of register spills on the 'fast-path' kernel. attaching quick notes.

maria: Ugh, that matches what I saw in the nightly perf dashboard. short-seq p95 went from 48ms -> 120ms for some workloads.

devon: Do we know which kernel variant got preferred? autoselector logs show it picked variant 'v8_unroll8_tile64' for compute SM80.

alex: Right — autoselect favored a high-occupancy variant that uses aggressive unrolling. That variant reduces cycles per-token on long sequences but uses ~64 regs/thread. Spills started appearing once batch mix had many short requests with small KV footprint.

ryan: Quick theory: for short-seq requests the KV cache path keeps more SMEM per warp, so effective registers+smem pushes threads over limit -> spills. Suggest adding an occupancy-aware cost term to autoselector that penalizes high-register kernels when smem footprint is nontrivial.

sara: Agree. Also the batching heuristic changed recently to co-batch more short requests which increases instantaneous warps. That multiplies the register pressure. We should test two knobs: tile_size (32 vs 64) and prefetch_count (2 vs 4).

perf-bot: nvprof snapshot: hot kernels: v8_unroll8_tile64 (regs=64, smem=8KB, occupancy=0.6), v6_unroll4_tile32 (regs=44, smem=4KB, occupancy=0.48). Spill stores increase 3x on v8 for seq<64.

maria: Can we land a short-term fix? My vote: change autoselector policy to prefer lower-reg variant for seqlen<128 by default. Also throttle co-batching of short requests until we validate.

devon: I ran a local patch that adds an effective_occupancy metric: effective_occupancy = min(occupancy, max_warps * (1 - smem_frac) * (1 - reg_frac)). It prioritized v6_unroll4_tile32 and p95 dropped back to ~55ms on my bench. Will push perf traces.

alex: Nice. Can you drop the trace here? Also let's add a regression test: synth load with 90% short (<64) + 10% long to ensure autotuner picks lower-reg variant.

devon: Dropping gist of experiment config:
```
{
  "gpu": "A100",
  "workload": {"short_pct": 0.9, "short_len": 32, "long_len": 1024},
  "variants": ["v8_unroll8_tile64","v6_unroll4_tile32"],
  "metrics": ["p50","p95","spill_stores","avg_regs"]
}
```

sara: FYI we should also check KV eviction policy — if prefetch_count is too high for short requests we end up thrashing the L2 and incurring extra latency. Maybe tune prefetch only for long-path kernels.

ryan: For long-term, propose autotuner evaluate kernel candidates across a weighted sequence-length histogram, not just average seqlen. Also expose a flag to bias toward 'min_spill' variant.

maria: Agreed. Action items: 1) devon open PR with effective_occupancy patch + regression test, 2) sara add short-co-batch throttle in batching heuristic, 3) alex update autoselect policy doc and add a 'seqlen-aware bias' toggle. I'll schedule a quick shiproom if needed.

alex: Thanks — if anyone can validate on V100 / T4 too that'd be great; different reg/smem tradeoffs there. I'll follow up with rollout plan. :thumbsup:
